tasks.title: Catch a note the browser reads as HTML
tasks.description:
Before you change anything, prove the hole. In `src/reproduce.js`, implement `reproduceNoteMarkup()`.

Make an order whose title, customer name or note holds text the browser reads as HTML, and run it through the original `renderOrderCard()`. Return an object with:

- `order`: `{ id, title, status, customerName, note }`, all three customer fields as strings
- `html`: exactly what `renderOrderCard(order)` returned

The check runs your function against the original `orderCard.js` and reads the card the way a browser would. It passes when `html` is real and the browser builds something other than what the customer typed.
nextSteps: Run `node src/demo.js` and compare order 2046's note with what the staff board shows.
Read `renderOrderCard` and see where each value lands.
Make an order whose note holds a tag of its own.
Run the demo again and read `tags` in what the staff board shows.
hints: Yusra's note on order 2046 already shows the hole. Look at what the staff board shows for it.
The browser reads every < in the card as the start of a tag, wherever it came from.
Copy order 2046 from the demo into an object, keep its note Size A2 <not A3>., and return it with renderOrderCard(order).

tasks.title: Write customers' words as text
tasks.description:
Fix `renderOrderCard(order)` in `src/orderCard.js` so whatever customers typed is shown exactly as they typed it, and never becomes HTML.

- The title, the customer name and the note each show as typed, in the note field too: angle brackets, ampersands and quotes included.
- No text from the order adds a tag or an attribute to the card.
- The HTML around the values stays the same.

The check renders cards with honest and unfriendly orders and reads each one the way a browser would, with `readCard()`.
nextSteps: List the characters that mean something in HTML.
Write a small function that turns each of them into its character reference.
Run every value through it where it goes into the HTML, the note field included.
Run `node src/demo.js` and check order 2046's note.
hints: The cause is that the customer's words are pasted into the HTML as they are. Removing characters changes what they wrote; the browser has a way to show any character as text.
Five characters need it: & < > " and '. Turn & into its reference first, or you will change the references you just wrote.
A function that returns String(value).replaceAll('&', '&') and so on for the other four, called on every ${...} in the card.

videos.title: How a page runs code it was sent

tasks.title: Write the test that would have caught it
tasks.description:
Write vitest tests in `src/orderCard.test.js` that guard this hole for good. Render cards with `renderOrderCard()` and read them back with `readCard()` from `staffScreen.js`.

The check runs your test file three times: beside the original `orderCard.js` (it must fail), beside a correct fix (it must pass) and beside a fix that escapes `<`, `>` and `&` but not quotes (it must fail).
nextSteps: Render a note with a tag in it and assert the browser shows it as text.
Add a case the fix without quotes gets wrong.
hints: readCard tells you the words in each part, the note field's value, the tags and any event attributes. Compare them with what the customer typed.
The fix without quotes keeps tags out, so a test with only a tag passes on it. Where does a quote matter in this card?
Put a note that holds a double quote in the order and expect readCard(html).noteField to be that exact note.
